title: Keep the repricing job away from frozen price books

blocks.text: The shop keeps one live price book and freezes a copy at every month-end, so that finance can replay that month's orders at that month's prices. In `PriceBooks`, a `FrozenPriceBook` is a `PriceBook` like the live one, and its `setPrice` throws.

Last month-end the repricing job was started against the frozen March book instead of the live one. The wiring compiled and passed review, and the job failed at run time on the first price it tried to change. Finish `src/main/java/practice/PriceBooks.java` so that:

items: `FrozenPriceBook.of(source)` freezes the prices the source answers at that moment; repricing the source later doesn't reach the frozen book;
handing a frozen book to `Repricer` is a compile error, not a run-time one;
finance's `Checkout` can still be built on a frozen book.

blocks.text: Leave `Repricer` and the three interfaces as they are. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: a frozen book answers the prices and skus its source answered when it was frozen, even when the source can only be read
repricing the live book after freezing it changes the live prices and leaves the frozen ones as they were
a frozen book has no price-changing role at all, so the repricer's constructor can't be given one
checkout depends only on looking prices up, so it totals a basket from a frozen book

origin.section: Role Interfaces Turn the Refusal into a Compile Error

concepts: A client that only reads takes the reading role, so it runs on implementations that can't write.
Splitting the interface into roles lets the read-only implementation drop its writer methods, so handing it to a client that writes no longer compiles.
An implementation that throws UnsupportedOperationException from a method of a fat interface compiles, and the wiring mistake that calls it fails only at run time.
